overview: The Old Kingdom is a phase of Egyptian civilization, approximately 2649-2130 BCE in the Met chronology. Royal building projects and elite tombs reveal changing institutions; funerary evidence disproportionately shapes modern knowledge.

items.text: Djoser’s Saqqara complex established monumental pyramid architecture. Under Snefru, builders developed smooth-sided pyramids.
Early royal administration concentrated high office among the king’s relatives. Later officials and provincial elites gained prominence.
Tomb reliefs depicted farming, hunting and food preparation. These were purposeful funerary images, rather than neutral records of everyday life.
Pyramid Texts appeared in Unis’s burial apartments and were adopted by later royal tombs.
Central authority fragmented as provincial governors became autonomous. The relative contributions of dynastic politics, decentralization and environmental pressure remain debated.

sources.title: Tara Prakash, Met, Egypt in the Old Kingdom
